sourceNote: All records curated from Wikipedia with coordinates verified against Wikipedia article geotags. Jodhpur is the second-largest city in Rajasthan. All records needs_review.

places.name: Mehrangarh Fort
places.description: One of India's largest and best-preserved forts, founded in 1459, rising 125m above Jodhpur on a rocky hill. Museum inside houses palanquins, elephant howdahs, royal cradles and armour. Offers sweeping views over the Blue City. Several palace rooms to explore; budget 2–3 hours.

places.name: Jaswant Thada
places.description: White marble cenotaph (memorial) built in 1899 for Maharaja Jaswant Singh II, located 1km from Mehrangarh Fort. The translucent marble glows golden at sunset. Surrounding grounds include a small lake, garden and royal portraits gallery. Far less crowded than Mehrangarh; combine as a half-day visit.

places.name: Umaid Bhawan Palace
places.description: One of the world's largest private residences, built 1929–1943. Split between a Taj hotel, the royal family's private residence and a museum wing open to visitors. The museum houses vintage cars, royal memorabilia and art deco furnishings. Exterior viewable from the gardens.

places.name: Clocktower and Sardar Market
places.description: The Ghanta Ghar (Clocktower) is the anchor of Jodhpur's old city market. Sardar Market surrounds it with stalls selling spices, fabric, handicrafts, snacks and silver jewellery. Best experienced in the morning before the heat; buzzing atmosphere in a historic setting. Free to enter.

places.name: Blue City Walk
places.description: The lanes of Jodhpur's old Brahmin quarter, where indigo-blue painted houses cluster below Mehrangarh Fort, are one of Rajasthan's most photogenic urban landscapes. Best appreciated on foot through the narrow streets near Navchokiya, Manak Chowk and surrounding mohallas. No single entry point; start from Clocktower or Fort base.
places.openingDays: Open all day; best light in early morning

places.name: Mandore Gardens
places.description: 9km north of Jodhpur, Mandore was the ancient capital of Marwar before Jodhpur. The gardens contain cenotaphs (memorials/chhatris) of the Jodhpur rulers, Hall of Heroes with rock-carved figures, and a small museum. Free entry; popular with domestic tourists. Quiet alternative to the crowded fort.

places.name: Balsamand Lake
places.description: 11th-century artificial lake 5km north of Jodhpur. The Balsamand Lake Palace (now a heritage hotel) sits at the water's edge surrounded by mango, papaya and date palm trees. Garden open to day visitors; pleasant escape from the city heat. Birdwatching site with migratory waterfowl in winter.

places.name: Toorji Ka Jhalra (Stepwell)
places.description: 18th-century baori (stepwell) recently restored to its original glory, located near Clocktower in the old city. Features geometric descending steps and ornate blue archways. One of the most photogenic stepwells in Rajasthan and a lesser-known attraction. Free entry; best photographed in early morning light.

places.name: Rao Jodha Desert Rock Park
places.description: 70-hectare ecological park at the base of Mehrangarh Fort, restoring the indigenous rocky scrubland ecosystem after decades of invasive plants. Guided trails through the rocky terrain with interpretation of local flora and desert plants. Entry fee; best combined with a morning Mehrangarh visit.

places.name: Kaylana Lake
places.description: Artificial lake 8km west of Jodhpur created in 1872, popular for sunset views, birdwatching and morning boat rides. Flamingos, pelicans and other migratory birds visit in winter. A relaxing half-hour stop on a day around the city.

places.name: Osian
places.description: Ancient town 65km north of Jodhpur containing a remarkable cluster of 8th–11th century Jain and Hindu temples. Often called the Khajuraho of Rajasthan; ornate carvings in sandstone. Can be combined with a visit to Sambhar Salt Lake or as a half-day excursion from Jodhpur.

places.name: Ghanta Ghar (Clocktower)
places.description: The historic clock tower at the heart of Jodhpur's old city, built by Maharaja Sardar Singh in 1880. Serves as a navigational landmark and the de facto entrance to Sardar Market. The surrounding area is lively morning and evening with local street food including makhaniya lassi.

places.name: Jodhpur Makhaniya Lassi
places.description: Jodhpur's signature thick saffron lassi topped with malai cream, famous at Shri Mishrilal Hotel near Clock Tower. Also try the ghee-laden pyaz kachori (onion pastry), mawa kachori, and mirchi bada at the stalls surrounding Sardar Market.

places.name: Jodhpur Rooftop Mehrangarh View Dining
places.description: Rooftop restaurants in the blue city below Mehrangarh Fort offer panoramic views of the indigo-painted houses and the fort at sunset. On the Rocks and Indique are popular for local Rajasthani cuisine with a stunning backdrop. Best visited at dusk.
